newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 4.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - In July government revenue exceeded spending by 6 billion crowns, thereby reducing the budget deficit by 8.8 billion. Were it not for serious flooding, the surplus could have beein higher by 773 million crowns.

- There was an unexpectedly large demand for flood bonds, with all banks reporting that their supply had been sold out when the bonds were introduced last Friday. The bonds were issued in 1,000 crown and 10,000 crown denominations.
- Filip sedivy, former Czech ambassador to Slovakia was elected chairman of the board by Unipetrol shareholders. Sedivy replaces Miroslav Tera as chairman. Rea, however, will remain on as CEO.

- Skoda Mlada Boleslav raised the sale price of its models effective August 4. The Octavia model's price was increased by 3.9 percent, while the retail price of all Felicia models have been increased by 3.2 precent.

- The Finance Ministry announced that no penalties will be levied against individuals who failed to meet tax and insurance payment schedules as a result of flooding. The ministry did say, however, that rescheduled payments will have to be met.

- Ceska Kooperativa, the second largest insurance company in the Czech Republic announced a profit of 42.5 billion crowns for the first half of 1997. The insurance company which enjoys a 9.8 percent market share has thereby more than doubled its year on year profits.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Industry and Trade minister Karel Kuhnl announced that his ministry estimates the direct cost of damage to industry in areas affected by flooding to be as high as 35 billion crowns.

- Government experts predict that the Czech pension system will last no longer than several decades if current trends continue. The experts attribute this forecast to an increasingly ageing population. If the trend continues, the experts say, the state deficit will reach 21 billion crowns by the year 2050.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The Blax Corporation continues in plans to manage Poldi Steel through September when it expects to manaufacture 5-8,000 tonnes of steel. Blax continues to negotiate with Mossei International Holding for the sale of 50.3 percent of shares in Poldi Steel.

- While private citizens are snapping up recently issued flood bonds, the same cannot be said for companies. The reason for this is that the bonds are not designed to raise a profit, and investors cannot see a return on their investment until five years time.

PRAVO - Ceska Posta announced 1996 revenues of 9.908 billion crowns, a year on year increase of over 1 billion. The post office also announced a profit of 461 million crowns, up from 403 million crowns in 1995.

- Frantisek Chvalovsky, chairman of the Hops producers association said that he will press for international quotas on the production of hops in individual countries. Chvalovsky will push for the declaration at the 45th international hops growers congress which begins in Prague on Aug 4.
